hardware.query: I want to build a physical controller for Flappy Bird where covering/uncovering a light sensor controls the bird.

facts.statement: ESP32 GPIO operates in the 3.3 V domain; use 3.3 V signals for direct GPIO input.
facts.beginnerExplanation: Do not send a 5 V sensor signal straight into an ESP32 pin.

facts.statement: ESP32 includes 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities.
facts.beginnerExplanation: The board can later communicate wirelessly without an extra radio module.

facts.statement: GPIO34 is ADC1 channel 6 and is input-only with no internal pull-up or pull-down.
facts.beginnerExplanation: GPIO34 is a verified analog input for the light sensor, but it cannot power anything and needs an external divider resistor.

facts.statement: Arduino Uno R3 has 14 digital I/O pins, 6 PWM outputs, and 6 analog inputs.
facts.beginnerExplanation: The Uno is easy to learn and has enough analog inputs for a light sensor.

facts.statement: Arduino Uno R3 operates with 5 V logic.
facts.beginnerExplanation: Its pin voltage is different from the ESP32, so sensor wiring cannot always be copied between boards.

facts.statement: The classic Arduino Nano ATmega328 is a 5 V board with analog inputs and PWM-capable digital pins.
facts.beginnerExplanation: The Nano is compact but uses the same 5 V logic family as the classic Uno.

facts.statement: Raspberry Pi Pico provides 26 multifunction GPIO pins, including 3 exposed ADC inputs, plus PWM, I2C, SPI, and UART.
facts.beginnerExplanation: The Pico can read a light sensor and control many common parts, but the base Pico has no built-in wireless radio.

facts.statement: Raspberry Pi Pico GPIO uses 3.3 V logic.
facts.beginnerExplanation: Keep signals connected to Pico GPIO at 3.3 V.

facts.statement: A photocell is read through an analog-input voltage divider; a 10 kilohm fixed resistor is a documented beginner starting value.
facts.beginnerExplanation: The LDR and 10k resistor turn changing light into a safe voltage the board can measure.

facts.statement: Fixed resistors are used for current limiting, pull-up or pull-down states, and voltage dividers.
facts.beginnerExplanation: The resistor value and its exact position are part of the circuit, not optional decoration.

facts.statement: A voltage divider creates a measurable midpoint voltage and can reduce a higher signal voltage for a high-impedance input.
facts.beginnerExplanation: Two resistive parts can turn a changing resistance or a higher signal into a safe input voltage.

facts.statement: Consistent wire colors make beginner circuits easier to inspect: red for power, black for ground, and another color for signals.
